title: The functor of maps from a product with a finite simplicial set is representable

standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial object and its category
standard_prerequisites.statement: A simplicial object is a contravariant functor from the simplex category; maps between simplicial objects are natural transformations, and X times U denotes the degreewise product.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the setting of the represented functor and of the degreewise analysis in the proof (source lines 1628-1640, 1644-1660).

standard_prerequisites.name: Coproducts and countable limits in the base category
standard_prerequisites.statement: The category C has coproducts of any two objects and limits of countable diagrams.
standard_prerequisites.use: The coproducts let the degreewise conditions be assembled and the countable limits are what guarantees the existence of the representing object (source lines 1628-1630, 1665-1674).

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of the simplicial set in each degree
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every U_n is a finite non-empty set.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the degreewise condition into a finite product indexed by the elements of U_n, which is what makes the limit countable (source lines 1630, 1646-1664).

core_obligations: Reduce to degreewise conditions: use the definition of maps of simplicial objects to express a map X times U -> V as a compatible family of maps in each degree, and use the finiteness of U_n to write the degree n component as a finite product indexed by the elements of U_n (source lines 1644-1660).

Identify the indexing category and the limit: collect the compatibility conditions into a small indexing category U built from the simplicial set and rewrite the functor as the limit of the induced diagram over the opposite of that category (source lines 1661-1670).
Conclude representability: invoke the hypothesis that C has countable limits to obtain the limit, and hence an object representing the functor (source lines 1671-1674).

proof_roadmap.step: Express a map X times U -> V by its degreewise components, using finiteness of each U_n.
Rewrite the functor as a limit over the small category built from U.
Use countable limits in C to produce the representing object.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-exists-hom-0-from-simplicial-set at source lines 1626-1641: if the category C has coproducts of two objects and countable limits, U is a simplicial set with every U_n finite and non-empty, and V is a simplicial object, then the functor sending X to the set of maps from X times U to V in simplicial objects is representable. The proof at source lines 1643-1675 is a two-stage reduction rather than an appeal to a stated theorem: it first rewrites the set of maps in terms of the individual degrees, using that U_n is finite to express the degreewise maps as a finite product indexed by the elements of U_n, which is where the finiteness hypothesis is consumed; it then rewrites the resulting condition as a limit over a small category built from U, and invokes the hypothesis that C has countable limits to conclude that the object representing the functor exists. The reader has to see that the finiteness makes the products finite and that the indexing category is countable, neither of which the statement spells out. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
